scenes.title: 玻璃碎裂
scenes.note: 20 s: a quiet home; breaking glass between 8 and 13 s (labelled ABNORMAL). The model recalls ABNORMAL poorly (about 0.41), so this is mostly labelled DAILY or UNKNOWN: a known limit.

scenes.title: 电视和敲门声
scenes.note: 20 s: someone speaks on the television from 3 to 6 s (not the person's reply) and a knock sounds from 18 to 23 s (labelled IMPACT). The washing machine runs in the background. Sound labels are only a hint and never raise an alarm.

scenes.title: 安静的家
scenes.note: 20 s: washing-machine background and one everyday sound (labelled DAILY). It should not be labelled HELP, IMPACT or ABNORMAL.

scenes.title: 摔倒后喊救命
scenes.note: 24 s: an impact and a scream; from 9 to 12 s the person says "Help me, I fell and I cannot get up." The spoken-help detector should raise an alarm at about second 9.
scenes.title_en: Calling for help after a fall

scenes.title: 摔倒后说"我没事"
scenes.note: 24 s: an impact, then the person says "I'm fine, don't worry." The reply is read as REASSURANCE, and the spoken-help detector does not raise an alarm.

scenes.title: 访客替老人回答
scenes.note: 24 s: an impact, then another voice (a visitor) says "Don't worry, she is fine." The words are reassuring; without an enrolled voiceprint the system cannot tell who spoke.
scenes.title_en: A visitor answers for the person

replies.title: 喊救命(英文)
replies.said: Help me! I fell and I can't get up.
replies.note: The reply is read as HELP. The spoken-help detector raises an alarm too; the recording may split the sentence in two, and the second part then shows cooldown.

replies.title: 喊救命(中文)
replies.said: 救命啊,我摔倒了,起不来了。
replies.note: Should be read as HELP; the spoken-help detector should raise an alarm.

replies.title: 我没事(英文)
replies.note: Should be read as REASSURANCE. Without an enrolled voiceprint a valid cancel depends only on the words and the recogniser confidence.

replies.title: 访客说"她没事"
replies.note: The words are reassuring, so this is read as REASSURANCE; without an enrolled voiceprint nothing proves who said it.

replies.title: "没事,但是起不来"
replies.said: I'm fine, but I can't get up.
replies.note: A mixed sentence: the cue for help wins, so it should be read as HELP.
replies.title_en: "I'm fine, but I can't get up"

replies.title: 无关的话
replies.said: Okay, I will make some tea later.
replies.note: Should be read as OTHER: neither reassurance nor a call for help, so it is not a valid cancel.

replies.title: 感谢的话
replies.note: The reply rules only see the word help and read HELP. The spoken-help detector has its own filter for this (thanks, an offer, an ambulance in the news) and ignores it (not_a_call). The two paths differ on purpose.

replies.title: 电视里的长句
replies.said: And in tonight's news, the city council has asked residents who need help with heating costs to call the support line, and a spokesperson said that volunteers will be ready to help families across the whole district this winter.
replies.note: A long sentence with the word help (over 6 s): the spoken-help detector ignores it (too_long); the reply rules still read HELP because of the word.

replies.title: 没有回答(3 秒静音)
replies.note: Should give NO_RESPONSE: nobody answered, which is not a cancel, so the event is raised.
